summary: Multi-tenant rebuild tested end-to-end. Backend: 14/14 new pytest tests pass (tests/test_multitenant.py). They cover the registry, the fleet lifecycle, chamber bounds, tenant isolation over REST and WS, MQTT payload validation and per-client mocked alarms. Frontend at 390x844: superadmin device-select, chamber tabs switching between K1..K6 and Komora 1..3, selection persisting after reload, the whole FleetCard flow, client-admin scoped UI, viewer read-only UI, AUTO/manual, Dane charts/daily usage/CSV link, setpoint +/-, threshold save, broker form and PL/EN. No horizontal overflow (doc width 390). One medium tenant-isolation leak found: when a deleted device_id is re-used for another client, the new client sees the old client's data.

minor.issue: TENANT LEAK on device_id re-use. delete_device only removes device_thresholds. plc_events, plc_history, plc_plant_history and alarm_active keys stay keyed by device_id. If the same device_id is re-created under another client, that client's users can read the old client's events through /api/events?device_id=X (the query matches by device_id only, not client_id). Reproduced: a client-B viewer saw 'Dodano sterownik: TEST_A_... / devA' and 'devA – Komora 1: progi ...' from client A. History, CSV and usage would leak the same way.

Generated mqtt_username/password are cosmetic on public HiveMQ: no ACLs, so anyone who knows the prefix can publish state or commands for any device. Expected for the MVP; enforcing them needs a private broker with an ACL plugin.
The user object is cached when the socket connects. Deleting a user or changing role/client does not affect an open WS until it reconnects (access token lifetime is 15 min).

ui_bugs.issue: After the selected device is deleted, the UI correctly falls back to devices[0], but localStorage 'device' keeps the stale id. Harmless.

issues: The new-user-role select cuts off 'Operator (sterowanie)' as 'Operator (sterc'
The K6 tab is cut at the right edge with no scroll affordance (fade or arrow). It scrolls correctly (scrollWidth 384 > clientWidth 360).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1016 lines, over the 700-line guideline. Split it into simulator.py, gateway.py and routes/*.
events(): `{'device_id': None, **q}` inside $or is fine. However, `{'device_id': device_id}` is not filtered by client_id, which causes the re-use leak above.
PATCH /devices/{id} with simulated=false keeps stale gateway.states, so the last snapshot is still served with online=false. This is acceptable, but consider marking it or clearing it.
sanitize_state casts float ids with int() (1.5 -> 1). Minor.
Old test files in /app/backend/tests (test_piggery_mqtt.py, test_iteration7/8/9*.py, restore_state_it8.py) target removed endpoints and will fail. Delete or update them.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=... pytest /app/tests/test_multitenant.py -v -p no:cacheprovider (prefer the /app/tests copy: editing files under /app/backend triggers a uvicorn reload and HiveMQ reconnect). The tests create and clean up their own data. The MQTT test publishes directly to broker.hivemq.com under prefix emgt-fatek-7f3a9c. probe_reuse.py reproduces the device_id re-use leak.
rca of the issue: Device re-use leak: history and event collections are keyed by device_id, and delete_device does not purge them. events() for a visible device queries {device_id: X} without a client_id filter, so leftover rows from the previous owner are returned. Mitigation: purge on delete, or add client_id to history docs and filter by it.
